extracted.intended_audience: mathematics researchers preparing submissions to the Annals of Mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research manuscripts to the Annals of Mathematics, covering submission channel and file formats, required items (abstract, bibliography), language, formatting, figures, references, and publication/copyright policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel and allowed submission formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be sent via email to the Annals editorial office at annals@math.princeton.edu. The submitted manuscript should be in the format of a PDF file attachment or an arXiv number from the Mathematics e-print arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may provide an arXiv identifier instead of a PDF. No special submission portal is required—email is the stated route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article processing charges
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no article publishing charges (APCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are not required to pay APCs for submission or publication in the Annals of Mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be written in English, French, or German.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission is not in English, then two versions of the abstract must be included: one in the language of the article and one in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI & LLM policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Annals of Mathematics does not consider papers generated using AI products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only individuals who can take full responsibility for the contents of a submission can be named authors. Authors must declare as supplemental information in the manuscript any use of AI or LLM and include the extent and purpose of such use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Only individuals who can take full responsibility for the contents of a submission can be named authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is linked to the AI policy and general ethical responsibility: authorship implies accountability for the manuscript's content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required items: abstract and bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of about 200 words or less and a bibliography must be included in a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should be self-contained and not make any reference to the bibliography. If the submission is not in English, include an additional English abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged formats and source submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to use LaTeX. The class file for the journal is aomart, available from CTAN. Authors are not required to format their files with aomart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper is accepted, authors will be asked to submit all source material by email to the Annals office. Authors whose papers are accepted may choose to format their final versions with the journal’s aomart.sty; information is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographical reference completeness and citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographical references should be complete, including article titles and page ranges. All references in the bibliography should be cited in the text. The use of BibTeX is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a paper is published, the references will include links to DOI, Math Reviews number (MR), and Zentralblatt MATH number. If a reference has not been published, include the arXiv number or a URL if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure quality and acceptable file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must be of publication quality. After acceptance, authors will need to submit the original source files in vector graphics format for all diagrams: vector EPS or vector PDF files are the most useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most drawing and graphing packages allow saving as vector EPS or PDF; ensure what is saved is vector graphics and not a bitmap. Authors are encouraged to bundle figure files into a single archive (zip, tar, rar, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure placement, captions, and small/inline figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each figure should be captioned and numbered so that it can float. Small figures occupying no more than three lines of vertical space can be kept in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is acceptable to submit a manuscript with all figures at the end if their placement is specified in the text by comments such as 'Place Figure 1 here.' The same considerations apply to tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: No forced line or page breaks / white space policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Forced line breaks or page breaks should not be inserted in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not attempt to control pagination with manual breaks; the production process will handle layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs and offprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Page proofs will be made available to authors in PDF format. Authors of accepted papers will receive 10 offprints and a copy of the published issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extra offprints may be purchased through the editorial office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and copyright/posting policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of papers which have been accepted for publication will be asked to sign a copyright agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can link to the publisher’s version of their articles as soon as they are available. As stated in the copyright agreement, authors of accepted papers can post PDF files of the final accepted version on personal webpages, electronic preprint servers, and institutional non-commercial repositories. Authors may attach a CC-BY license only to the accepted version that resides in an open access environment such as arXiv or a personal webpage; the CC-BY license is not applicable to the version published by the Annals of Mathematics.
